newsitem.title: USA: Debt sales on deck for Arkansas Dev. Fin. Auth..
newsitem.headline: Debt sales on deck for Arkansas Dev. Fin. Auth..

text.p: The Arkansas Development Finance Authority may sell a $50 million to $60 million housing bond deal next month as well as a $25.5 million Department of Corrections refunding, authority officials said Tuesday.

Goldman Sachs & Co will underwrite the single-family housing bond issue, which the authority hopes to sell "around the end of February," Charles Brandt, the authority's bond funds administrator, said.

Arkansas Development sold its last housing bond issue--$50.5 million of convertible option bonds--in mid-November, Brandt said. The authority plans to remarket about $18 million of that earlier issue as part of the planned $50 million to $60 million sale, he said.

As for the $25.5 million Corrections Department deal, Gene Eagle, an Arkansas Development Authority vice president, said proceeds will be use to refund a $22.845 million corrections department offering priced in 1990. Both the refunding and the previous issue are have MBIA Insurance Corp insurance. Goldman Sachs & Co and Morgan Keegan & Co Inc will act as co-senior managers, Eagle said.

Looking ahead, the authority may also sell about $15 million of new bonds under it's ecomomic development program, he said. The authority has its own guarantee program, and recently issued an $11.165 million refunding deal, which is expected to close soon. The refunding bonds were also AMBAC insured, Eagle said.
The deal refunded an offering done on behalf of 13 companies that approached the authority seeking funds for economic development back in the late 1980s, he said.

The authority will probably issue a few series of college savings bonds, and while amounts of those issues have yet to be decided, they will likely be between $15 million and $25 million each, Eagle said. How many series of college savings bonds the authority issues, "really depends on the market for the bonds," he said.
"I mean we have averaged about almost three or four series a year," Eagle said. "We would want to do up to $100 million, that's how much authority we've got left."
The Development authority also handles the leveraging of the state revolving loan fund for waste water and clean water, he said.
"I expect that there will be another leveraging package put together sometime this year," Eagle said, adding that the amount of bonds sold under that package has yet to be determined.
